etymologies.etymologyHTML: Recorded in Middle English c. 1410 as retreve (altered to retrive in the 16th century; modern form is from c. 1650), from Middle French retruev-, stem of Old French retrover (“to find again”, modern retrouver), itself from re- (“again”) + trover (“to find”), probably from Vulgar Latin *tropāre (“to compose”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To regain or get back something.

quote.citation: 1697, Virgil, “The Sixth Book of the Æneis”, in John Dryden, transl., The Works of Virgil: Containing His Pastorals, Georgics, and Æneis. […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: With late repentance now they would retrieve / The bodies they forsook, and wish to live.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To fetch or carry back something, especially (computing) a file or data record.

quote.citation: 1714, Rev. Dean Berkeley, letter to Alexander Pope, May 1, 1714:
quote.text: to retrieve them from their cold, trivial conceits

definitions.definition: (transitive) To fetch and bring in game.
(intransitive) To fetch and bring in game systematically.
(intransitive) To fetch or carry back systematically, notably as a game.
(sports, transitive) To make a difficult but successful return of the ball.
(obsolete) To remedy the evil consequence of, to repair (a loss or damage).

quote.citation: 1718, Mat[thew] Prior, “Solomon on the Vanity of the World. A Poem in Three Books.”, in Poems on Several Occasions, London:  […]  Jacob Tonson […], and John Barber […], →OCLC, (please specify the page):
quote.text: Accept my sorrow, and retrieve my fall.

quote.citation: 1795–1797, Edmund Burke, “(please specify |letter=1 to 4)”, in [Letters on a Regicide Peace], London: [Rivington]:
quote.text: There is much to be done  […]  and much to be retrieved.

definitions.definition: (sports) The return of a difficult ball
(obsolete) The recovery of game once sprung.

quote.citation: 1625 (first performance), Ben[jamin] Jonson, The Staple of Newes. […], London:  […]  I[ohn] B[eale] for Robert Allot […], published 1631, →OCLC, (please specify the page), (please specify the scene number in lowercase Roman numerals):
quote.text: we'll bring Wax to the retrieve
